episodes.158515: A few thunderstorms produced sporadically gusty winds near the middle portion of the Chesapeake Bay.
episodes.158550: A thunderstorm moved south near the coast in central Brevard County and produced strong wind gusts over the Indian River Lagoon and adjacent land areas.
episodes.158764: A severe thunderstorm produced large hail over golf ball size for a prolonged period east of Martin.
episodes.158765: A thunderstorm briefly became severe over eastern Haakon County, producing wind gusts to 60 mph.
episodes.158838: An area of high pressure stayed centered over the Four Corners while above normal moisture values also continued across New Mexico on July 4, 2021. A weak disturbance rounding the high pressure and moving southward from Kansas into eastern New Mexico and the Texas Panhandle allowed for increasing instability, wind shear, and lift that resulted in a few strong to severe thunderstorms across the eastern plains for the Independence Day holiday. Hail sizes were generally sub-severe while the Tucumcari airport measured the strongest wind gust of the day with 63 mph. Meanwhile, strong to severe winds in Roosevelt County resulted in minor property damage.
episodes.159083: Severe thunderstorms moved across portions of Scotts Bluff and Sioux Counties on the fourth producing hailstones up to one inch.
episodes.159085: A severe thunderstorm moved across Goshen County producing hailstones up to one inch in diameter.
episodes.159555: A surface front across SE Georgia brought moist, deep layer WSW flow across NE Florida. An upper level trough axis extended from the SE Atlantic coast to across the FL panhandle. Training bands of showers and storms moved across the local area, enhanced by several mid-level vorticity maxima that streamed over the area.
episodes.160020: Isolated thunderstorms produced large hail and a brief tornado across parts of northwest Nebraska, primarily Sheridan and Cherry Counties, the evening of July 3.
episodes.160207: A compact short-wave trough moved over central North Dakota resulting in thunderstorm development. Instability was elevated and deep layer shear was marginal. This was enough, though, for large hail to develop over parts of the James River Valley. The largest hail was the size of a ping pong ball, which occurred northeast of Napoleon in Logan County.
episodes.160317: A plume of monsoon moisture extended across the region and thunderstorms were ongoing in the morning of the 4th due to an Mesoscale Convective Vortex (MCV) moving southeast from the northeast Texas Panhandle into western Oklahoma.  An upper level short wave moving south through western Kansas along with a surface trough across northeast New Mexico into the western Oklahoma Panhandle helped to spark additional showers and thunderstorms in the northwest during the afternoon hours. Thunderstorms, some severe, and some with excessive rainfall developed across the western Oklahoma Panhandle and the northwest Texas Panhandle during the mid afternoon given moderate instability in the area.  These thunderstorms moved south-southwest across the western Panhandles.  Hail up to 2 inches in diameter and flooding was reported near Dalhart.  Winds up to 78 mph were reported at the Boise City mesonet station and severe wind gusts were also reported at several other ASOS ad mesonet stations across the area. Additional thunderstorms with damaging winds developed after midnight across the south central and southwest Texas Panhandle and moved southwest.
episodes.160775: A high-based thunderstorm collapsed near the Southwest Wyoming Regional Airport just east of Rock Springs and produced a 58 mph wind gust.
episodes.160861: Severe thunderstorms produced damaging winds, large hail, and two weak landspouts over Logan, Morgan and Washington counties.  Large hail, up to ping pong ball size and wind gusts to 60 mph, caused minor tree damage.
episodes.160863: Isolated  thunderstorms developed across portions of Douglas, Grand and Morgan counties.  Microburst winds damaged boats on Grand Lake.  One pontoon boat was lifted off the water and landed upside down near a home.  In Larimer County, a brief period of heavy rain caused minor flash flooding in the Cameron Peak burn area near Glen Haven, along Miller Fork.  In Douglas County, nickel size hail was observed.  Lightning sparked a small grass fire near Wiggins in Morgan County.
episodes.160959: Strong thunderstorms developed in the afternoon over the high terrain of central and southern Arizona before spreading to the lower deserts through the evening, with new development driven mostly by strong outflow boundaries. The primary outflow boundary moved southwest with widespread 30-40 mph wind gusts observed across south-central Arizona and a few stronger gusts, including a 59 mph gust in southern Gila county. The winds were strong enough to cause hundreds of power outages in the Phoenix metro area and generate dense blowing dust over the open deserts in Pinal and western Maricopa counties. With above normal moisture levels, storms also produced localized flash flooding mostly in foothill/high terrain areas, including flash flooding enhanced by recent burn scars.
episodes.160968: Thunderstorms developed along a stationary front in a very moist airmass. Some on these storms produced heavy rain that led to flash flooding.
episodes.160978: Low level moisture remained across the Sacramento Mountains which combined with a weak upper level disturbance to create some slow moving thunderstorms.  One storm dropped 1.50 inches of rain 5 miles west of Mayhill which caused some mud to cross Highway 82.
episodes.161150: A cluster of supercell thunderstorms developed along a boundary in Northwest Kansas and moved west. These storms produced up to golf ball sized hail and up to 90 MPH wind gusts. The strongest winds occurred in northern Gove County where a large evergreen tree was uprooted.
episodes.161458: An isolated severe thunderstorm near Eldorado produced a wet microburst which resulted in wind gusts of 75 to 85 mph and some wind damage.
episodes.161570: Isolated showers and storms occurred along the I-25 corridor during the afternoon on this day, especially around and north of Pueblo. There was additional development across the eastern plains, but both areas really only observed isolated severe storms.
episodes.161571: Isolated thunderstorm development was once again noted across the eastern plains on this day, with a few strong to severe storms producing large hail and heavy rainfall with flash flooding.
episodes.161677: The combination of a weak stationary front and abundant tropical moisture resulted in showers and thunderstorms that produced some localized flooding mainly in San Angelo and Abilene.
episodes.161867: A mid-level trough pushed across much of the western half of the CWA.  Ample instability with moderate CAPE and moderate mid-level lapse rates gave way to a number of hail reports up to the size of golf balls and damaging winds up to 65mph.
episodes.162430: An active surface trough moved over the territory on the weekend of July 4th. This feature produced widespread impacts of flash flooding, coastal erosion, and landslides.

events.narrative: Significant amount of flowing water through Icehouse Canyon and Pinal Creek in Sixshooter Canyon, with downstream flow through Globe, was observed due to heavy rain. Runoff was enhanced by the recent Telegraph burn scar. A spotter in the area reported all major creeks and washes were flowing with ash blackened flood waters. The spotter added that Beer Tree Crossing through Sixshooter Canyon was flooded and there was minor street flooding further downstream. No damages or injuries were reported.
Strong winds downed tree branches.
Report posted via social media.
Large branches broken. Metal roofing bent up on building.
A few large 3 to 5 inch diameter tree branches broken.
Peak wind measured at an NDAWN station at 3 meters.
Public reported hail ranging from dime size up to golf ball size.
Hail larger than golf ball size fell for about 45 minutes. Wind gusts to 50 mph also accompanied the storm.

An emergency manager reported a 4-5 foot rise in water in the typically dry Russell Gulch with enhanced runoff from the 2021 Telegraph burn scar. The timing of max flow was estimated.  Additionally, Russell Road, which runs through Russell Gulch, was reportedly closed at mile marker 4 by a former trained spotter due to flood waters and burned mud. No damages or injuries were reported.
Peak wind measured at a personal weather station.
Peak wind measured at a personal weather station.

events.county: Tangier Sound And The Inland Waters Surrounding Bloodsworth Island
events.narrative: A thunderstorm produced an estimated wind to 34 knots (39 MPH) near a mesonet near Crisfield.
A trained weather spotter reported 1.25 inch hail (estimated).

A Twitter video showed an estimated 6 inches of flowing water over Bush Highway and roughly 3 feet of water collected on the side of the highway at about 1 mile north of the Butcher Jones turnoff. No damages or injuries reported.

Upper Campaign Creek rose 1 to 2 feet. Runoff may have been enhanced by the 2019 Woodbury burn scar. Low water crossing along J Bar Road closed due to flowing water and debris. Time estimated from radar and nearby NWS rain gage. No damage or injuries were reported.
Pea sized hail also fell with the storm.

Tonto National Forest closed Butcher Jones Beach Road due to significant flash flooding impacts to the recreational beach and day-use area. Time estimated by radar. No damages or injuries were reported.
Storm total rainfall was up to 3.31 inches since midnight. About 1.18 inches occurred in the past hour.

Arizona Department of Transportation (ADOT) reported via Twitter that the flood prone state route 238 was closed in both directions between mile markers 25 and 38 due to flooding. The Twitter report was roughly 2 hours after the causative heavy rain. Timing was adjusted based on radar. Radar estimated rainfall was around 1.00-1.25 inches. ADOT reported state route 238 reopened at 20:15 on the 4th. No damages or injuries were reported.
Heavy rainfall of 1.34 inches, most of which occurred within 30 minutes.

WSO Pago Pago recording 1.40 inches of rain within a 24 hour period. Though it doesn't seem as much, flash flooding was reported in the harbor area where the Siufaga National Park Site recorded 6.26 inches of rain. Cars were submerged in water in the front of the Pago Pago Catholic church, a low-lying area. A major landslide was also reported in the village of Aua in the front of the Tilo's residence.
Strong microburst winds damaged several boats at Grand Lake.  Two large pontoon boats were lifted out of the water, one landed upside down near a home.

Thunderstorms produced heavy rain that led to flash flooding in northern Austin. A video on Twitter showed up to six inches of water on roadways at the intersection of Shoal Creek Blvd. and Hancock Blvd. along Shoal Creek.

Law Enforcement reported a wet microburst winds of 75 to 85 mph which ripped a metal roof and some siding off a residence and also damaged a roof from a nearby barn. The damaging winds also broke some tree limbs.
An inch and a half to 2 inches of rain fell just west of Mayhill which caused some mud to come across Highway 82.
A car was stranded in flood water near the intersection of Flagler Ave and Land Ave in San Marco.

Larimer County Sheriff reported flash flooding near Glen Haven.  An estimated 1.2 inches of rain fell in one hour.  The areas around Steamside Drive and Fishermans Lane just north of Glen Haven were most impacted by floodwaters from Miller Fork.
Caller reported various sized hail, mostly pea to dime in size with a few quarter sized stones mixed in.
A power pole was blown down by the high wind.
Street flooding was reported in and around the city of Dalhart. Roads did remain passible.
Caller reported a full grown evergreen tree was uprooted as a strong supercell moved over the location.
Storm chaser reported 1-2 inch diameter hail in and around Dalhart to around 5 miles north of town. Some minor accumulating hail was reported on highway 385, about 4 miles north of the city as well.
An NWS Employee reported 2 to 3 inches of water covering the road.

events.county: Volusia-Brevard County Line To Sebastian Inlet 0-20Nm
events.narrative: A mesonet site along US Highway 1 in Palm Shores, just south of the Pineda Causeway recorded a peak wind gust of 39 knots from the north-northwest as a strong thunderstorm moved down the Indian River Lagoon and adjacent land areas.
A strong thunderstorm near Wagon Mound produced nickel size hail as it tracked southward through the area.
A trained spotter reported 3 inches of water covering Avenue N by Angelo State University.
An Amateur Radio operator reported water over the road on College Hills at the Red Arroyo.
Report received of 1 to 1.5 inch hail falling for around 2 minutes.
Winds were estimated to be 60-65 MPH.
A 58 mph wind gust was measured by ASOS at Southwest Wyoming Regional Airport.
Winds were estimated to be at least 60 MPH.
The public reported flooding on Ranch Road 783 just south of US 87.
Lightning sparked a grass fire.
Hail up to 2 inches broke storm chaser's windshield.
